text: The paragraph contains a factual error regarding legal compliance. The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) generally covers service animals, which are dogs (or in some cases miniature horses) that are individually trained to do work or perform tasks for people with disabilities. Emotional support animals (ESAs) are not considered service animals under the ADA. However, housing providers are required to make reasonable accommodations for ESAs under the Fair Housing Act (FHA), not the ADA. Therefore, stating that the landlord kept in compliance with the ADA by making exceptions for emotional support animals is legally inaccurate; the compliance stems from the FHA.
